subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the unit vector perpendicular to the plane passing through the points (1,2,3), (2,−1,1) and (1,2,−4).

mark_split.label: Find two vectors in the plane
Cross them to get a normal

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.63 — SAQ chapter 9 Product of Vectors, answer 59. Printed appearances: AP 17 · TS 22. The answer carries a ± sign, and that is not optional: a plane has two unit normals, one on each side, and both are correct.THE MARK SPLIT IS PRINTED in that book's margin as [1 Mark] against each of four working lines — a sourced 1+1+1+1 — a sourced split, not an inference. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q13 is the Product of Vectors slot.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find a unit vector perpendicular to a plane through three points.

steps.label: Find two vectors in the plane
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both from the same point A. AC comes out as a pure k vector here, which makes the cross product short.
lines: OA = i + 2j + 3k, OB = 2i − j + k, OC = i + 2j − 4k

recall.must_convey: That two vectors lying in the plane, AB and AC, are built from the same point A.
accept: find AB and AC from the same point A, both lie in the plane
take two vectors in the plane from one of the points
AB is OB minus OA and AC is OC minus OA which is minus seven k
A nunchi rendu vectors, avi plane lo untai
build two in plane vectors from one vertex

steps.why: Any two non-parallel vectors lying in the plane determine its direction completely — which is what makes their cross product a normal to it.
common_mistakes: Using the position vectors themselves rather than differences.
Missing that AC has only a k component.

steps.label: Cross them
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The cross product of two vectors in the plane is perpendicular to the plane. Taking 7 out makes the next two steps easy.

recall.must_convey: That the cross product AB×AC gives a normal to the plane, here 21i + 7j = 7(3i + j).
accept: cross them to get twenty one i plus seven j which is seven times three i plus j
the cross product is perpendicular to the plane
AB cross AC gives the normal, take seven out
cross product plane ki perpendicular, seven common teeyyochu
the normal vector is seven into three i plus j

steps.why: A cross product is perpendicular to both its factors. Since both factors lie in the plane, the result is perpendicular to the whole plane.
common_mistakes: Taking a dot product, which gives a number and no direction.
Missing that the k component is zero.

steps.label: Find its magnitude
steps.margin_note: Third mark. With the 7 already outside, only 3² + 1² has to be squared — a much smaller sum than 21² + 7².

recall.must_convey: That the magnitude is 7√10, with the 7 kept outside the root.
accept: the magnitude is seven root ten
with seven outside it is seven times root of nine plus one
seven root ten is the modulus
seven root ten vasthundi
take the magnitude keeping the seven outside

steps.why: A positive factor outside a vector comes straight outside its magnitude, which is why factoring first is worth the extra line.
common_mistakes: Squaring 21 and 7 and then failing to simplify √490.

steps.label: Divide, keeping ±
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 7 cancels top and bottom. Keep the ± — a plane has a normal on each side and the question did not say which.

recall.must_convey: That dividing the normal by its magnitude gives ±(3i + j)/√10, and that the ± must be kept.
accept: divide to get plus or minus three i plus j over root ten, and keep the plus minus
the unit normal is plus or minus three i plus j by root ten
a plane has two unit normals so the answer carries plus or minus
plus or minus three i plus j by root ten, rendu vaipula normals untai
the seven cancels leaving plus minus three i plus j over root ten

steps.why: Reversing a normal still leaves it perpendicular to the plane, so both signs are genuine answers. Dropping the ± gives only half the answer.
